parameters.name: include_events
parameters.description: Backend clients must opt in to event actions; defaults to false (cron-only).

409.description: Configuration changed or execution is active
Configuration changed or execution is active

503.description: AI usage validation unavailable; retry later

409.description: The routine was edited after activation

AccessLevel.description: Ordered from least to most access top -> bottom

ActionConfiguration.description: Canonical client configuration. Ownership and execution state are server-owned.

run_visibility.description: Omitted by clients that predate the setting; runs then start unlisted.

ActionConfigurationUpdate.description:
Canonical configuration replacement. Activation has its own endpoint, so
omitting `enabled` keeps the stored value; omitting `run_visibility` keeps
it too, so clients that predate the setting do not reset it.

enabled.description: Still sent by clients deployed before the activation endpoint.

resource_id.description:
ID of the primary resource produced by this run. Its type is recorded in
`result`, independently of the routine's current configuration.

ActionTrigger.description: A routine may run on one trigger or any of several schedules and Macro events.

oneOf.description: Absent when using Macro's agent-session runtime with a selected model.
Required for model targets; overrides the persona default for agent targets.

AgentTaskAgent.description: A persona selection, independent of its runtime and current default model.

AiAdmissionErrorBody.description:
Public admission error payload. Handlers with additional fields can reuse the
domain error's code and message and [`admission_status`].

error.description: Human-readable explanation, without internal billing diagnostics.

BindingProblem.description: One variable that can't be used as given.

oneOf.description:
A channel, document, email thread or call. `name` is the label its
mention shows; access is always checked by `id`.

BoundValue.description: A value for one variable: fixed by the creator, or chosen at activation.

access_level.description: The access level for the channel

oneOf.description: The triggering content answered the condition with no.

probability.description: The classifier's probability, from 0 to 1, that the answer was yes.

oneOf.description: The condition could not be checked before the retry window closed.

ConditionResult.description: Why an event-triggered run was skipped before it started.

CreateScheduledAction.description: Exactly one representation is accepted, even if mixed fields agree or are null.

EmptyResponse.description: Empty response is required due to custom fetch forcing `response.json()`

EventFilter.description:
An event name AND an entity ID must match within the same filter. A
condition further requires the event's content to answer it with yes.

condition.description:
Yes/no question about the triggering content, e.g. "Is this email an
invoice?". The routine runs only when the answer is yes.

EventFilters.description: Bounded nonempty OR of filters, canonicalized to remove duplicates.

EventName.description:
Closed allowlist: unknown names, deletions and ambiguous attribution are not
selectors. Adding a broker variant does not automatically enable routines.

ExecutionResource.description: Transcript resource created by a run. Never infer this from current task configuration.

ExecutionResourceType.description: Closed set of transcript destinations understood by routine clients.

ExecutionResult.description:
Version 1 execution metadata stored in the existing JSON result column.
Null/string column values predate this envelope and refer to legacy chats.

oneOf.description: Present when an event trigger's condition stopped the run from starting.

ExtractedTemplate.description:
A routine's draft template for its owner, plus the template they
already made from it so the dialog can offer to update or reuse it.

Extraction.description:
A proposed template plus the creator's own value for each variable. The
values go back to the creator only, so the share dialog can switch a
variable to fixed; they are never stored for variable slots.

current.description: The viewer's current choices, so related variables change together.

instruction.description: "Do this for Initech instead": re-fill with this instruction.

name.description: A routine name using the filled values, e.g. "Weekly Globex digest".

FilledVariable.description:
One variable after fill and validation. `value` is absent when nothing
usable was found; `problem` then says why.

oneOf.description: Absent only in responses from legacy workers.

LegacyActionConfiguration.description: Deprecated cron-only input, accepted during the compatibility rollout.

LinkShare.description: Defines who can access an item through its share link.

RoutineModelId.description: A nonblank model identifier. Runtime catalogs, not the scheduler, own availability.

RoutineProvenance.description: The template a routine was activated from, for the routine's owner.

rebindable.description:
Whether the routine still reads exactly as the template rendered it,
so a single binding can be changed.

oneOf.description: Absent when the template is gone or no longer shared with the owner.

variables.description: The template's variables, for labelling the bindings.

RoutineProvenanceResponse.description: The template a routine came from; absent for a routine made by hand.

source_action_id.description: The routine it was made from. Absent once that routine is deleted.

RoutineTrigger.description: An individual trigger in a routine's trigger list.

RoutineTriggers.description: Bounded schedules and one combined set of event filters.

RunVisibility.description:
Whether a routine's runs are listed in Home and the Agents list. Routines
that run often would bury the owner's own work, so runs start unlisted;
either way they stay in the routine's history. The string form is the
`scheduled_action.run_visibility` column's.

enabled.description:
When false, automatic dispatch skips this action. `run_now` remains
available regardless.

event_activated_at.description: Event publication boundary; absent for cron actions.

next_run_at.description: Next cron firing, absent for event-triggered actions.

owner.description:
Who the action belongs to. Every action is user-owned today, but the
type no longer says so: the principal string on the wire and in the
`owner` column is the same, and a bot- or team-owned row decodes
rather than failing to parse.

run_visibility.description: Whether the action's runs are listed in Home and the Agents list.

schedule.description: Deprecated: use `trigger.schedule`. Present only for cron actions.

timezone.description: Deprecated: use `trigger.timezone`. Present only for cron actions.

ScheduledActionResponse.description:
Canonical trigger plus deprecated cron fields for existing clients. Event
responses omit legacy fields rather than inventing a schedule or timezone.

ScheduledActionUpdate.description:
Live status update for a scheduled-action run, broadcast via the connection
gateway to the owner. Clients use the typed resource to navigate to the run
transcript and the variant tag to toggle the running indicator. `chat_id`
remains populated only for chat runs, for older clients.

Serialized with a `type` tag (`started`/`stopped`) and delivered over the
single `scheduled_action_update` message type on the gateway.

channelSharePermissions.description: The channel share permissions for the item

oneOf.description: Who can access the item through its share link
The level of access granted through the share link
The explicit access level granted to the owner's team, or `null` when disabled.
Overrides the agent's default model.

TaskTarget.description: The agent or model a routine runs on.

TemplateBindingErrors.description: Why the given bindings can't be used, per variable.

TemplateDraft.description:
Everything a template holds except identity and bookkeeping. This is what
extraction proposes, the creator edits, and activation renders.

TemplateEventFilter.description:
An event filter whose ids may be variables. Filters without ids are
already relative to whoever owns the routine.

TemplateRoutineTrigger.description: One entry of a template's trigger list.

TemplateTask.description: The routine's task with its target replaced by the agent variable.

user_prompt.description:
Markdown instructions with `<m-template-variable>` nodes in place of
person-specific values.

TemplateTrigger.description:
A routine trigger with variables where values would appear. Mirrors
`ActionTrigger`; a cron entry's schedule and timezone are one variable.

TemplateVariable.description: A named slot in a template.

description.description: One line, written for the person activating the template.

your_activations.description: Routines the viewer activated from this template.

TemplateView.description:
A template as a viewer sees it. Never holds the creator's values for
variable slots, because the template never stores them.

oneOf.description:
The access level for the channel
This is required if the operation is add or replace

operation.description:
The type of operation to be performed on the chanel share permission
You can add, remove or replace and existing permission

UpdateScheduledAction.description: Full replacement of client configuration, not of server-owned action state.

channelSharePermissions.description: Any channel share permissions to be created/updated/removed

oneOf.description:
Who can access the item through its share link. Omit to leave unchanged or pass `null` to
disable link sharing.

The link access level. Omit to leave unchanged or pass `null` to reset it to the default
level when a link share exists.

The explicit team access level. Omit to leave unchanged or pass `null` to disable team
sharing. Only the actual owner may change this setting; `owner` is not an allowed level.

VariableKey.description: A stable slug naming a variable within one template: `urgent_channel`.

oneOf.description: The routine's target: an agent, or a model on Macro's runtime.
A cron schedule and its timezone.
Free text, such as a company or an email domain.
An email thread or call watched by an event trigger.

VariableKind.description: What a variable stands for, and so which picker fills it.

VariableMode.description:
Whether each activator fills a variable in, or everyone gets the
creator's value.

VariableRef.description: `{"$var": "<key>"}`: where a template holds a variable instead of a value.
